alignments.note: Hebrew writes a connective of its own for each member, so each takes only the English word written for it and there is no correlative pair to place (rule 14).
The indefinite article belongs to the nominal (rule 15).

Articleless attributive recast as a relative clause keeps the supplied relative with the attributive itself (rule 41), headed on the lexeme-bearing *superfluous*; the unit is discontinuous around the supplied verb under rule 25.

Nothing in the clause makes it possessive — no היה, no possessive preposition and no suffix — and the participle still keeps *superfluous* when the word is dropped, so the supplied *hath* answers to no morpheme and is added together with the object noun the English formula requires (rules 20, 43), exactly as *hath its stones* is at v24. Rule 41 licenses an articleless attributive's relative and any copula rule 20 supplies, not a possessive verb. Keeping *hath anything* inside the participle's own multi-word rendering under rule 31 was the competing reading, and is what the earlier alignment took.
The ASV writes *or* for this waw (rule 14).
The second attributive keeps only its own English, the relative being written once across the pair (rule 22).
The ASV supplies both the preposition and the head noun for a phrase the Hebrew never writes, so the whole supplied phrase is its own added unit (rules 30, 33).
A bare nominal with no preposition and no object marker on it takes the supplied *for* itself (rule 33); head on *freewill*, since *offering* alone is any offering (rule 31).
The verb takes its subject pronoun and auxiliary (rule 17).
Object marker with no English of its own (rule 16).
The suffix's pronoun is realized by the fronted demonstrative (rule 18).
The ASV writes *but* for this waw (rule 14).

review_notes: Corrected: the supplied *hath* is not licensed by rule 41, which gives an articleless attributive its relative and any copula rule 20 supplies. Nothing in this clause makes it possessive and the participle keeps *superfluous*, so under rule 43's closing test *hath* and the object noun *anything* it requires are added together; the participle keeps the discontinuous *that ... superfluous*.
*in his parts* stays added: the Hebrew writes neither the preposition nor the dimension noun (rules 30, 33).
Each member of וְשׁוֹר וָשֶׂה has a connective of its own, so *Either* and *or* are taken separately and rule 14's correlative pair is not placed.
